paper.title: Sequential Test for the Lowest Mean: From Thompson to Murphy Sampling

settings.name_in_paper: Sequential test of mu* < gamma vs mu* > gamma (one-parameter exponential family arms)
unmapped: delta-correct sequential test of whether the minimum mean is below or above a known threshold gamma
the learner knows the threshold gamma
settings.definition_quote: Given a threshold $\gamma \in \cI$, our goal is to decide whether $\mu^* < \gamma$ or $\mu^* > \gamma$. ... We aim for a \emph{$\delta$-correct} algorithm, that satisfies $\pr_{\vmu} \del*{\vmu \in \mathcal H_{\hat m}} \ge 1-\delta$ for all $\vmu \in \H$.

settings.name_in_paper: Sequential test for the lowest mean, Gaussian case (analysis of LCB)
unmapped: delta-correct sequential test of whether the minimum mean is below or above a known threshold gamma
the learner knows the threshold gamma
settings.definition_quote: For simplicity we only consider the Gaussian case, in which confidence intervals have the stylized form $[\LCB_a(t), \UCB_a(t)] = \sbr*{\hat \mu_a(t) \mp \sqrt{\frac{2 \ln \frac{1}{\delta}}{N_a(t)}}}$.

source.quote: Any $\delta$-correct strategy satisfies \eqref{eq:gen.lbd} with T^*(\vmu) = ... \sum_a \frac{1}{d(\mu_a, \gamma)} if \mu^* > \gamma

conditions: bound holds for every arm a

source.label: prop:impbinf
source.quote: Let $k  = \max_a d(\mu_a,\gamma)$. For any symmetric, $\delta$-correct test, for all arms $a\in\{1,\dots,K\}$, \[\ex_\vmu[N_a(\tau)]\geq \frac{2\left(1-2\delta K^3\right)}{27K^2k}\;.\]

results.notes: Lower bound on expected number of draws of each arm (quantity other).

symbols.d_1: d(mu_1, gamma) with mu_1 the smallest mean

source.label: th:impbinf
source.quote: When $\mu^* < \gamma$, for any symmetric, $\delta$-correct strategy, \ex_{\vmu}[\tau] \geq \frac{\kl(\delta, 1-\delta)}{d(\mu_1,\gamma)} + \frac{2\left(1-2\delta K^3\right)}{27K^2k}\sum_a \left(1-\frac{d_+(\mu_a, \gamma)}{d(\mu_1,\gamma)}\right)

conditions: any anytime sampling strategy ensuring N_t/t -> w*(mu)
stopping rule tau_delta <= Box stopping rule with thresholds non-decreasing in r and C(delta,r) <= f(delta) + ln r for r >= r0, f(delta) = ln(1/delta) + o(ln(1/delta))

source.label: lem:asym.smp.cplx
source.quote: Fix $\vmu \in \H$. Fix an anytime sampling strategy ($A_t$) ensuring $\frac{\bm{N}_t}{t} \to \w^*(\vmu)$. Let $\tau_\delta$ be a stopping rule such that $\tau_\delta \leq  \tau_\delta^\BoxStop$, ... Then $\lim\sup_{\delta \to 0} \frac{\tau_\delta}{\ln \frac{1}{\delta}} \le T^*(\vmu)$ almost surely.

results.notes: Lemma 4 is generic for any sampling rule converging to w*; Theorem 5 shows MS satisfies this (under bounded parameter space and bounded prior density ratio assumptions), giving asymptotic optimality of MS with Box/Aggregate stopping. Attributed to MS here.

tuning: subset prior pi summing to 1; threshold T(ln(1/(delta pi(S))))

source.quote: Any algorithm using the stopping rule $\tau^\pi$ and selecting $\hat m = \ >$ iff $\tau^\pi = \tausup$, is $\delta$-correct.

conditions: Gaussian arms with stylized confidence intervals

source.label: prop:LCB.good
source.quote: There is a function $\epsilon_\delta \to 0$ decreasing as $\delta \to 0$ such that for every $\vmu \in \Hsup$ \lim_{\delta \to 0} \pr_\vmu \del*{ \frac{\tau_\delta}{\ln \frac{1}{\delta}} \le (1+\epsilon_\delta) T^*(\vmu)} = 1.

results.notes: Holds with probability tending to 1. Proof uses stylized confidence intervals (footnote admits these are not exactly correct and approximations ignored).

source.quote: There is a function $\epsilon_\delta \to 0$ decreasing as $\delta \to 0$ such that for every bandit model $\vmu \in \Hinf$ with $\mu_1 < \gamma < \mu_2 \le \ldots$ ... \lim_{\delta \to 0} \pr_\vmu ( \forall a \neq a^*(\vmu) : \frac{N_a(\tau)}{\ln \frac{1}{\delta}} \ge (1-\epsilon_\delta) \frac{2}{(\mu_a + \gamma - 2 \mu_1)^2} ) = 1.
